prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Katy, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1057; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the parking lot collision you were involved in. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident itself, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. For the record, can you confirm you were the driver of the vehicle you were operating at the time?

A: Yes, I was driving my own car.

Q: Where exactly did the collision happen?

A: It was in a shopping center parking lot in Katy, near the main entrance. I was backing out of a space in one of the front rows.

Q: What were the weather and lighting conditions?

A: It was daytime and clear. The lot was pretty busy, so there were a lot of cars moving around.

Q: Walk me through what happened when the impact occurred.

A: I checked my mirrors and started reversing slowly. I didn't see the other vehicle coming down the aisle until it was right there. We hit on the rear passenger side of my car.

Q: Did you have any contact with the other driver at the scene?

A: Briefly. They said they were looking at their phone and didn't see me pulling out.

Q: Were you injured?

A: Yes. I put my right hand out to brace myself when the airbag went off, and my wrist took the force. I was taken to the emergency room that afternoon, and they told me it was fractured.

Q: Are you currently receiving treatment for that wrist?

A: I have a cast and I'm seeing an orthopedic specialist. I'm supposed to go back for a follow-up in a few weeks.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about how the accident happened?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to make sure my medical bills and the car repairs get taken care of.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the recorded statement.
